one_month_reasoning: No ALAB print in the window: the Q3 2026 report date is still unannounced as of Sep 30 (search of IR news releases), and last year's Q3 came in early November, so expect ~Nov 3-5. Inside the window: hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary in the last week of October (two-sided; no capex cuts announced so far), OCP Global Summit in October (mildly positive product/design-win flow), the Oct 28 FOMC with ~69-73% odds of a 25bp hike (Kalshi; CNBC Sep 23; mostly priced but asymmetric to a hawkish surprise for a ~56x P/E name), and OpenAI's widened training pause (second in three months, no restart date, Sep 28), a sentiment overhang of the kind that cost ALAB 10% on Sep 14. Versus round 1 I remove the small positive drift and centre slightly below spot (median ~$356) with ~25% monthly sigma; the scheduled events are sentiment rather than estimate movers, so I keep the spread near symmetric.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%): Sep-2027 NTM EPS ~$8.0 x 45x = $360, and EV/sales (40%): NTM revenue ~$3.6B x 17x + ~$2.0B net cash over ~190M diluted shares = $333; blended ~$349, slightly below today's $358.

ALAB trades ~56x 2027 consensus today and at 71x NTM EV/EBITDA vs Marvell 34x/Broadcom 20x (Jul 2026). Base rate: hyper-growth semis de-rate as growth decelerates from >100% to ~30%; Credo's multiple compressed ~50% peak-to-trough in 2026. 45x is a midpoint between today's premium and large-cap AI semi peers. The AWS warrant (vests on up to $6.5B of cumulative purchases through 2033) supports multi-year AWS engagement but is a ceiling, not a committed order book, and is contra-revenue; with top-3 customers at 69% of Q2 revenue it argues against paying a higher multiple, so I keep 45x rather than raising it.

bear.story: AI capex digestion or a sentiment shock (SOX fell 29% from its June peak; OpenAI's widening training pause; Polymarket 35% US recession by end-2027) with the Fed hiking into hot inflation. Concentration bites: AWS (warrant-linked, top-3 customers 69% of revenue) double-sources scale-up switching via NVLink Fusion/UALink competitors or Broadcom scale-up Ethernet, growth slows toward 20% and the multiple compresses to ~25-30x ~$6 EPS. Precedent: ALAB -68% Jan-Apr 2025; Credo -52% in 2026.

base.story: Scorpio X ramp and PCIe 6 keep revenue near or above the $2.97B 2027 consensus; EPS beats modestly, but the multiple de-rates from ~56x to ~45x forward as growth decelerates with hyperscaler capex (+22-29% in 2027). The stock ends near today's level with large swings on the way.

bull.story: Capex surprises high (Goldman $1.4T 2027 hyperscaler capex), Scorpio becomes a standard scale-up fabric across several custom-accelerator programs including UALink-native Trainium4 racks, AWS purchases track toward the warrant milestones, and 2028 EPS runs toward $11-12 with the market keeping ~55x. The stock clears the $499 high.

thesis_break_reason: About 40% below today and below the ~$250-290 lows of the July 2026 sector selloff that happened with fundamentals intact. At ~$212 the stock is ~33x 2027 consensus EPS of $6.39, which would most likely mean the market has priced a lost or double-sourced Scorpio socket at AWS (the customer behind the warrant and much of the 69% top-3 concentration), a Q4 guide at or below the Q3 ~$550M level, or real hyperscaler capex cuts rather than sentiment swings.

reasoning: Base rates first. ALAB is a ~$65B, 99%-realized-vol AI connectivity stock that has already done -68% (Jan-Apr 2025), a run to ~$499 and a ~40% drawdown (Jun-Jul 2026) with fundamentals intact; Credo fell ~52% from its high in 2026 and the SOX up to 29% from its June peak. I use a lognormal-ish distribution with sigma ~0.72 and fat tails. Round-2 checks against the supervisor: (1) the tail: P(>=89) of 0.965 put only 3.5% on a -75% outcome; given ALAB's own -68% in three months and Credo's -52%, I fatten it slightly to 4% below $89 and 10.5% below $143 (a -60% year), which still keeps the extreme tail thinner than the drawdown history alone would suggest because the business is now profitable with ~$1.25B cash. (2) Net cash: H1 2026 OCF was only $162M during the working-capital build, so I cut horizon net cash from $2.5B to $2.0B; EV/sales value falls $335->$333 and blended fair value $352->$349. (3) AWS warrant: confirmed it is a vesting ceiling on up to $6.5B of purchases through 2033, not an order book; it is both support for multi-year AWS demand and a confirmation of concentration, so I keep the 45x multiple and 25% bear weight rather than moving either. (4) Polymarket 'AI bubble burst' is loosely defined, so I drop it as an input and use it only as colour; the verified Kalshi Fed odds and the Polymarket recession market stay as macro context. (5) OpenAI's widened training pause and the ~70% Oct Fed hike are sentiment/multiple risks, not estimate risks (no hyperscaler has cut capex). Net: median moves from ~$362 to ~$358 (spot), fair value ~$349, scenarios $170/$365/$640 at 25/50/25 (probability-weighted mean ~$385), and the 1-month ladder loses its small positive drift. I disagree mildly with lowering the median further: the Q3 guide (+40% q/q) runs ahead of the 2027 consensus trajectory, which offsets the de-rating risk.
